BMW M3 Electric Spied on Video in the Open, Neue Klasse Model Expected in 2027
6 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | PrototypeHunters
BMW continues to tap deeper into the electric game, and one of the upcoming models that will feature a zero-emission powertrain will be the M3 .
Mind you, one should not mistake it for the next-gen ICE-powered BMW M3, which will sit at the very top of the new-gen G5X lineup, utilizing an updated version of the CLAR platform. That’s because the first-ever BMW M3 Electric will be the range-topping version of the new i3, and it is based on the same Neue Klasse architecture.
The model will look very similar to its gasoline-fed sibling, as both feature influences from the BMW M Concept Neue Klasse . Nevertheless, that does not mean that the body panels will fit both models, as these will be different. After all, we are talking about vehicles based on different constructions, and with completely different powertrains.
We have encountered the BMW M3 Electric on numerous occasions over the last few months, with the prototypes gradually adding their final bits and pieces ahead of the production kick off. The video embedded at the bottom of the page puts the spotlight on several testers, revealing how they have evolved with each passing encounter, with an obvious emphasis on some of the details inside and out.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | PrototypeHunters Signed by PrototypeHunters and shared on YouTube recently, the footage is a little over 11 minutes long, and it represents a great dive into the first-ever BMW M3 Electric. Thus, if you want to see it from numerous angles, and listen to what it sounds like, then you have come to the right place.
However, before inviting you to scroll down and click the play button, we also have to delve into the electric powertrain . Well, as much as we know about it, anyway, and the only fact at this point is that it will utilize a four-motor setup. The total output and thrust have not yet been officially confirmed, but reports indicate that we might be looking at 850 metric horsepower combined. That’s 838 horsepower for the brake crowd, equaling 625 kilowatts.
It will be interesting to see whether the German automaker has an even punchier version of the BMW M3 Electric on the table, because the platform is said to easily support electric powertrains with a four-digit output. However, in the meantime, we still have to see this model in all its glory, and chances are we are a few months away from its official premiere, which is expected to be hosted sometime in 2027, with the first units likely making their way to dealers in the USA for the 2028 model year.
BMW is also working on the M4 Convertible Electric , and so far, we have encountered it on two occasions. As for the ICE-powered next-gen BMW M3, this model is understood to come out in 2028.
